- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, cap the overshoot at 2–3% above recent peak.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) environments, model often underestimates downward moves; add 2–5% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.4.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong move, adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of prior 18-day history.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% in 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is low and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize the trend; forecast should be 1–2% below true outcome for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows a sharp drop from high to low, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day delay in price reversal.
